correctness.rationale: For one-ball initial masses, the probability of a count vector is n!/(d)_n, exactly uniform across C(n+d-1,d-1) weak compositions. Counting the marginal and joint zero/r events gives w_r/(u v_r)=(d-2)(d+n-1)/((d-1)(d+n-r-2)). Subtraction gives the local sign and summing off-diagonal while noting the forbidden diagonal gives the aggregate sign. Denominators are positive for d>=3,1<=r<=n, including n=1 and r=n. A separate exact-rational enumeration validated 330 triples and direct Pólya transition recursions validated 18 small instances. The proof, not finite tests, establishes the universal claim.

value.rationale: Empty colors and frequency classes are natural occupancy statistics. Their local and global covariance signs differ structurally because same-category empty-positive-frequency events are impossible; this creates a provable interval of opposite signs, a rational example, and infinitely many exact cancellations. The full finite-sample classification distinguishes reinforced sampling from the independently assigned occupancy model and supports interpretation of frequency-spectrum dependence. Its scientific value is an exact naturally motivated sign theorem, not merely numerical recomputation or a routine renaming.
